description:
He doesn't just break out of a dungeon. He builds a new prison for everyone who put him there, with a ledger in one hand and a blank check in the other.

In this deep dive into The Count of Monte Cristo by Alexandre Dumas, we read the novel as a financial thriller: a young sailor, a letter that burns, fourteen years in the Château d'If, and a Count who audits his enemies the way a banker audits bonds. We cover the betrayal in Marseille in 1815, Abbé Faria's education in the dark, the treasure of Monte Cristo, the market and telegraph games in Paris, and the cost of the revenge. We end on the book's own two words: wait and hope.
